To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) we have successfully developed and implemented a treebank-based algorithm for automatic f-structure generation and extraction for Chinese; (2) we have successfully extracted wide-coverage, lexical and grammatical resources from our f-structure- annotated treebank; (3) the automatically induced grammars are of high coverage, and perform well in terms of f-score on unseen data; and (4) we have demonstrated how to scale constraint-based, wide-coverage grammar acquisition to new languages and domains
we have developed a method for the automatic f-structure analysis of Chinese text that yields a high degree of coverage and a high degree of accuracy.

we have successfully induced a wide-coverage, LFG-based Chinese grammar from the Penn Chinese treebank, achieving 81.57%, 86.06%, and 73.97% f-score against unseen test data for tree, dependency, and predicate identification respectively.
In summary, our research is concerned with

(1) the development and evaluation of an automatic f-structural annotation algorithm for Chinese, (2) the development and automatic induction of a wide-coverage, LFG-based Chinese lexicon, (3) the development and induction of LFG-based PCFGs for Chinese, and (4) the development and application of an evaluation methodology for the automatic induction of wide-coverage, PCFG-based LRGs.
the following questions: (i) How well do our automatically induced grammars scale to unrestricted text?
scaling constraint-based, wide-coverage grammars from fragments to naturally-occurring unrestricted text.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we have successfully scaled the LFG framework from fragments to the Chinese Treebank.

our best automatic grammars achieve a reasonable degree of accuracy in terms of both f-structure and predicate-argument structure prediction, but that they do not yet perform well enough to be useful as a stand-alone resource for Chinese.
our best automatically induced LFG approximations perform well, but not yet as well as our manually developed LFG approximations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the results obtained are very encouraging, but that the induced grammatical resources still require a significant amount of manual post-processing.
our best automatic LFG grammars are competitive with the gold-standard f-structure annotations in the CTB, but that there is still room for improvement.
the results are encouraging, but the task of inducing wide-coverage, accurate LFG resources from treebanks remains difficult.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Penn Chinese TreeBank is a valuable resource for Chinese LFG grammar development and that our automatic f-structure induction algorithm can be used to bootstrap the acquisition process.

, in contrast to previous studies, we are now able to automatically acquire LFG grammars from a Chinese treebank, and that our results are promising in the sense that the automatically induced grammars perform comparably with those obtained for English and German, even though the treebank is much smaller and the grammar development environment much more challenging.
the Penn Chinese TreeBank is sufficiently rich to support automatic induction of wide-coverage, PCFG-based LCFG grammatical and lexical entries.
